title: Do not access freed memory
summary: Dereferencing a pointer after the allocated storage has been deallocated leads to undefined behavior, potential arbitrary code execution, or information disclosure.

title: Properly deallocate dynamically allocated resources
summary: Deallocating a resource using the wrong deallocation function (e.g. using free() on new, delete on new[], or failing to close handles) results in undefined behavior or heap corruption.
noncompliantCode:
int* arr = new int[100];
delete arr; // NONCOMPLIANT: Array allocated with new[] must be freed with delete[]
compliantSolution:
auto arr = std::make_unique<int[]>(100);
// Or prefer std::vector<int> arr(100);

title: Do not create cyclic primitive references in smart pointers
summary: Circular references between std::shared_ptr instances prevent the reference counts from ever reaching zero, leading to permanent memory leaks.

title: Do not depend on the order of evaluation of subexpressions
summary: Relying on the order of evaluation of function arguments or operands causes platform-dependent behavior and subtle bugs across compilers.

title: Do not read uninitialized memory
summary: Reading an object that has indeterminate value produces undefined behavior, leaking residual stack/heap data or corrupting computation.

title: Do not access an object outside of its lifetime
summary: Returning or retaining pointers/references to local automatic variables or expired temporaries results in dangling references and undefined behavior.

title: Do not access a value through an incompatible type
summary: Casting pointers between incompatible non-char types and dereferencing them violates the strict aliasing rule, allowing the compiler to optimize out stores.

title: A lambda result must not outlive captured references
summary: Capturing variables by reference ([&]) in a lambda that escapes the enclosing scope leads to use-after-free when the captured variables are destroyed.

title: Do not access the bits of an object through memcmp/memcpy if type is non-trivially copyable
summary: Using memcpy, memset, or memcmp on non-trivially copyable types (classes with virtual functions, std::string, etc.) corrupts internal pointers and vtables.
compliantSolution:
std::string s1 = "hello";
std::string s2 = s1; // COMPLIANT: Uses copy constructor

title: Do not rely on the value of a moved-from object
summary: A moved-from object is in a valid but unspecified state. Accessing its contents or assuming specific invariant values leads to undefined or unexpected behavior.

title: Guarantee that container indices and iterators are within valid range
summary: Indexing a container beyond its bounds with operator[] produces undefined behavior. Unlike .at(), operator[] does not perform bounds checking.
noncompliantCode:
std::vector<int> vec = {1, 2, 3};
int val = vec[5]; // NONCOMPLIANT: Undefined behavior, out of bounds

title: Use valid references, pointers, and iterators to reference elements of a container
summary: Mutating a container (e.g. push_back, insert, erase) can invalidate existing iterators and references, leading to use-after-free upon reuse.

title: Do not abruptly terminate the program with std::abort or std::exit from destructors
summary: Calling exit() or abort() skips pending RAII destructors, leaving files unflushed, locks unreleased, and resources uncleaned.

title: Do not throw an exception from a destructor or deallocation function
summary: Destructors in C++11 and newer are implicitly noexcept. Throwing an exception during stack unwinding immediately invokes std::terminate().

title: Catch exceptions by lvalue reference
summary: Catching exceptions by value slices derived exception classes into the base class, discarding derived state, error diagnostics, and polymorphic behavior.

title: Do not destroy a mutex while it is locked
summary: Destroying a locked std::mutex produces undefined behavior according to the C++ standard and POSIX threads specification.

title: Prevent data races on shared memory
summary: Concurrent access to non-atomic shared variables where at least one thread performs a write without synchronization causes undefined behavior.
compliantSolution:
std::atomic<int> counter{0}; // COMPLIANT: Atomic load/store with standard memory orders
++counter;

title: Avoid deadlock by acquiring locks in a consistent order
summary: Acquiring multiple mutexes in inconsistent orders across different threads leads to classic AB-BA circular deadlocks.
noncompliantCode:
// Thread 1: m1.lock(); m2.lock();
// Thread 2: m2.lock(); m1.lock(); // NONCOMPLIANT: Deadlock potential
compliantSolution:
// COMPLIANT: Use std::scoped_lock (C++17) to atomically lock multiple mutexes
std::scoped_lock lock(m1, m2);

title: Wrap condition variable waits in a while-loop
summary: Operating systems can wake up condition variables without notification (spurious wakeups). Testing the predicate with 'if' instead of 'while' causes invalid execution.
compliantSolution:
std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(m);
cv.wait(lock, [&ready] { return ready; }); // COMPLIANT: Predicate overload loops internally

title: Do not invoke virtual functions from constructors or destructors
vulnerability: Unbound Virtual Dispatch / Pure Virtual Call Crash
summary: During constructor and destructor execution, dynamic dispatch resolves only to the current class being constructed, NOT the derived class. Calling a pure virtual function aborts the program.

title: Do not slice derived objects
summary: Passing a derived class by value into a parameter of base class type slices off all derived state and virtual function table bindings.

title: Do not delete polymorphic objects with non-virtual destructors
summary: Deleting an object through a pointer to a base class that lacks a virtual destructor leads to undefined behavior and leaks derived class resources.

title: Do not use std::rand() for security-critical applications
summary: std::rand() produces predictable sequences of pseudo-random numbers with small periods (typically 32 bits), making cryptographic tokens or session keys trivially guessable.
noncompliantCode: int token = std::rand(); // NONCOMPLIANT: Predictable linear congruential generator

title: Value-returning functions must return a value on all control paths
vulnerability: Undefined Behavior via Missing Return Statement
summary: Reaching the closing brace of a value-returning function without an explicit return statement is undefined behavior in C++.

title: Do not define a C-style variadic function
summary: C-style variadic functions (...) provide no compile-time type safety, allowing arguments to be mismatched against format specifiers, resulting in memory corruption.
noncompliantCode: void log_msg(const char* fmt, ...); // NONCOMPLIANT: Type unsafe
